package_info.package_versions: before 4.45.07 (specifically, vulnerabilities confirmed in versions before 4.45.03 and 4.45.07)
package_info.why_malicious: The package contains multiple critical web application vulnerabilities (Reflected XSS, CSRF, and OS Command Injection) that allow attackers to bypass parental controls, escalate privileges, and execute arbitrary code on the server. These flaws enable a local or remote attacker (including children with access) to fully compromise the intended security boundaries of the application.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (HTTP GET request to admin panel)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code injects arbitrary JavaScript into the admin panel by reflecting unsanitized user input from the 'cat' query parameter, leading to execution in the parent’s browser and potential credential/session theft.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Reflecting unsanitized user input into HTML output enables arbitrary script execution, a classic XSS vector.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal behavior would sanitize or encode user input before rendering; here, user input is directly echoed.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Dynamic page titles or content based on user input, but always with proper encoding.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (HTTP POST request, can be triggered via XSS or crafted web page)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: var xhr=new XMLHttpRequest(); xhr.open("POST", "https://admin.ct.local/index.php?dgfile=privileged%20group/", true); xhr.setRequestHeader("Content-Type", "application/x-www-form-urlencoded");xhr.send("chk-2%3don%26choix%3dchange_user");
malicious_snippets.code_language: javascript (injected via XSS or external site)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code sends a forged POST request to the admin panel to change user privileges, exploiting the lack of CSRF protection to escalate privileges or disable filtering.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Critical state-changing actions are performed without verifying the request origin or requiring a CSRF token.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal admin actions should require anti-CSRF tokens and not be triggerable by third-party sites or scripts.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: AJAX-based admin actions, but always with CSRF protection.
key_indicators: No CSRF token in form or request
Can be triggered by XSS or external site

execution_context.trigger: runtime (HTTP GET request with crafted 'cat' parameter)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code concatenates unsanitized user input into a shell command executed by PHP’s exec(), allowing arbitrary OS command execution as the web server user.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: User input is directly concatenated into a shell command, enabling command injection and arbitrary code execution.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal behavior would validate and sanitize file names, never allowing user input in shell commands.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: None; file operations should always use whitelisting and never allow user input in shell commands.
key_indicators: Directory traversal and command injection possible

attack_chain.action: Attacker crafts a malicious link or web page exploiting the reflected XSS vulnerability to execute arbitrary JavaScript in the admin’s browser.
attack_chain.leads_to: Ability to steal session cookies or perform further actions as the admin.

attack_chain.action: Attacker uses XSS or a crafted web page to send a forged POST request to the admin panel, exploiting the CSRF vulnerability to escalate privileges or disable filtering.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker (child) gains privileged access or disables parental controls.

attack_chain.action: Attacker crafts a file with a malicious name and uses directory traversal and command injection to execute arbitrary OS commands as the web server user.
attack_chain.leads_to: Full compromise of the server with www-data privileges.

behavioral_signatures: Reflected user input in HTML output without encoding
Sensitive admin actions performed via POST without CSRF tokens
Shell command execution with user-supplied parameters
file_indicators: gctoff.php or index.php forms lacking CSRF tokens
Unusual files in /tmp/ with command-like names
network_indicators: Unexpected POST requests to /index.php?dgfile=privileged group from admin sessions
GET requests to bl_categories_help.php with suspicious 'cat' parameters (e.g., containing <script> or directory traversal sequences)
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for HTTP requests to admin endpoints with suspicious parameters (e.g., 'cat' containing script tags or directory traversal). Inspect POST requests to sensitive endpoints for absence of CSRF tokens. Audit server logs for command injection attempts and unexpected file access patterns. Use web application firewalls (WAF) to block reflected XSS and command injection payloads.
